import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/coffee_sales.csv')

# --- Data Preparation ---
# Convert date and time to datetime objects
df['datetime'] = pd.to_datetime(df['date'] + ' ' + df['time'])
df['hour'] = df['datetime'].dt.hour

# Group data by hour and product to get total sales
hourly_sales = df.groupby(['hour', 'product'])['total'].sum().reset_index()

# Find the top 5 products by total sales to keep the visualization clean
top_products = df.groupby('product')['total'].sum().nlargest(5).index
hourly_sales_top5 = hourly_sales[hourly_sales['product'].isin(top_products)]

# Pivot the data for heatmap representation
heatmap_data = hourly_sales_top5.pivot_table(index='product', columns='hour', values='total', fill_value=0)

# Reorder index based on total sales for better visual flow
heatmap_data = heatmap_data.loc[top_products]

# --- Visualization ---
# Set the style and create the figure
sns.set_theme(style="white")
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(16, 8))

# Create the heatmap
sns.heatmap(
    heatmap_data,
    annot=True,
    fmt=".0f",
    cmap="viridis",
    linewidths=.5,
    ax=ax,
    cbar_kws={'label': 'Total Sales ($)'}
)

# --- Customization and Labeling ---
# Set titles and labels
ax.set_title('Peak Sales Hours for Top 5 Products', fontsize=20, fontweight='bold', pad=20)
ax.set_xlabel('Hour of the Day (24-hour format)', fontsize=14, labelpad=10)
ax.set_ylabel('Product', fontsize=14, labelpad=10)

# Improve readability of ticks
ax.tick_params(axis='y', labelrotation=0)
ax.tick_params(axis='x', labelrotation=0)


# Adjust layout
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the final figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
